Freefield

Open-source Higgsfield on ComfyUI: every app is one folder, every model is open weights.

 Watch the 2-minute demo video 

 

Image, video, VFX and audio apps in a studio laid out like Higgsfield's, each one a ComfyUI workflow on open weights,
run on Modal, on a GPU rented by the hour (RunPod, Vast.ai) or on your own ComfyUI. Every example in the app is a real GPU run made by the lab, with its time and peak VRAM.

Run it on RunPod or Vast.ai, on Modal or on your own GPU · every app with its model and VRAM · add an app from any ComfyUI workflow ·
every GPU run of the lab

 
 
 Explore. Featured apps, the studios, and one lab example per app. 
 An app. The form is drawn from the app's app.json ; "Load this example" fills it with a lab run. 
 
 
 The Video menu. 46 apps grouped as in Higgsfield, and the open models behind them. 
 How it works. Every model with its size and license, the VRAM per phase, and the commands to run the app. 
 
 

Freefield rebuilds Higgsfield's creative apps (image, video, VFX, audio) on top of ComfyUI and the Comfy SDK.
There is no per-app code. Each app is a folder in apps/ with an app.json manifest and a ComfyUI workflow in API
format; the web UI, the runner, the model downloads, the VRAM map and the tests are all derived from those manifests.

 

 

 Sponsors

Freefield runs open-weights models on your own GPU and stays free. Sponsors help keep it going; their text is their own.

 
 
 
 Infistar.cc · Sponsored 
Stop overpaying for AI: up to 99% off official API prices. 100% genuine models for text, image and video, one API key.
Freefield users: get CNY 5 free through this link. 
 
 

 One click on RunPod or Vast.ai

No install and no Modal account. Rent a GPU with Freefield's public template: it starts the backend and the studio,
downloads the models of the default packs (64 apps, 22.9 GB) and prints a link to open.

 Deploy on RunPod Rent on Vast.ai 
 --- --- --- 
 1. Hugging Face token (once: accept the FLUX 3 license first) Settings → Secrets → hf token , with your read token Account → Environment Variables → HF TOKEN 
 2. GPU 24 GB or more, CUDA 13.0 or newer, and not a V100 (CUDA 13 dropped it). An L40S (48 GB) runs every app 24 GB or more, CUDA 13: the link opens Search with these filters set. Sort by price 
 3. Storage Add volume → Volume disk , 60 GB at /workspace : the deploy page does not add it by itself 60 GB, already in the template 
 4. Open it Logs: Freefield is ready on RunPod , with the link and its passcode View instance logs → Refresh: a trycloudflare.com link with its passcode 
 5. When you are done Terminate the pod Destroy the instance 

The first start takes 5 to 10 minutes: the image, then the models. Anyone with the link can use your GPU, so share it
only with people you trust. Other packs, a volume that outlives the pod, and what to do when something fails are in
the guide.

Both are referral links. They cost you nothing: RunPod and Vast.ai give Freefield a share of the credits, which pays for
the lab's GPU runs.

 Status

 
 --- --- 
 Apps 120: 119 ready (39 apps with a workflow of their own, the 5 IC-LoRA apps ( genjutsu , reframe , sdr-hdr , mixed-media , dub ), morph , 72 template apps (a fixed prompt over one of those pipelines, written by tools/template apps.py ) and 2 model-free smoke apps) and moss-image as a draft. The 118 that use models each have a lab example made on a GPU 
 Open weights No API or partner nodes. Every model is a file you download, listed in its app's app.json with its Hugging Face repo, size and license; the cloud text-encoder branch of Lightricks' examples is removed 
 Workflows Built from official sources by tools/build apps.py (ComfyUI's templates, Lightricks' ComfyUI-LTXVideo examples, Comfy's comfy-reshoot ); the template apps reuse those bases and the two smoke apps are hand-written. tools/import workflow.py drafts a new app from any other ComfyUI workflow. All accepted by ComfyUI's validator: ComfyUI e3bee7f (0.42.0), ComfyUI-LTXVideo 44c8a36 , ComfyUI-CrossViewWarp fbb1e93 
 GPU runs 48 lab runs on Modal from 20 to 26 Oct (L40S and H100), 710 of 733 cases ok. Every example in the web UI comes from one of them, with its time and peak VRAM. Run by run, and what each one changed: docs/lab-runs.md 
 End to end Run from the browser on 23 Oct, web UI → server → gateway on Modal → ComfyUI on an H100: morph 160.8 s from the button to the video (128.7 s of it on the GPU), mixed-media 149 s, dub 72 s. On 24 Oct through the hosted demo ( infra/web app.py , the same web app on Modal behind a passcode): face-swap 25.2 s on the GPU. The model-free smoke apps cover the same path in CI 
 LoRA lab 334 cases with fixed seeds: one showcase per app (117), 42 references the other cases start from, and experiments, each with its verdict in its note: every effect, look of mixed-media and transformation of morph on its own, the character types of ai-influencer , the image-model comparison ( cmp- , below), template and style-drift tests ( tplx- , mmx- ), reshoot without its Turbo LoRA, the soundtrack candidates for the demo video and checks of new controls. How the lab works: below 
 CI .github/workflows/validate.yml on every push: the manifest validator, the tests, the type check, the generated packs and VRAM map, and a CPU-only ComfyUI that accepts every workflow and the prompt of every lab case (about 3 minutes) 

 Apps

 App Rebuilds Model On a 24 GB card Status

 create-image Create Image FLUX 3 Image Klein (int8) + BFL's 9B prompt upsampler (an on/off toggle): 10 aspect ratios, 1K to 2K, 17 photographic looks; a layout table in JSON can follow the prompt fits whole, 17.8 GB ready 
 z-image Create Image, fast drafts Z-Image Turbo (int8); the lab makes its reference photos with it fits whole, 12.2 GB ready 
 moss-image Create Image with a layout MOSS-Image SFT (int8), Apache-2.0; also takes a layout JSON with a box per text and object fits whole, 13.0 GB draft
